title: Review of c09's AC-gel cells negative: replicated on fresh seeds 7 and 8; a fine a_th scan finds the all-or-nothing edge at a_th 0.35-0.45, where 1-4 discrete cells live about 100 time units before a boom into a sea that eats its substrate and dies
summary: Re-ran c09's world.py unchanged (only a_th varied) on fresh seeds 7 and 8. Scan a_th 0.10-0.45 in 0.05 steps, T=200, both seeds (scan_ath.txt): a_th <= 0.35 ends as one domain-filling cell (cell fraction 1.0 by t=40), a_th >= 0.45 (and the default 0.5) has no cells by t=10-20, so 14/16 runs are all-or-nothing as claimed. At a_th=0.40 both seeds sit on the edge: 2-4 discrete round cells with a gel focus inside at t=10-35 (rerun/p040_s7/sheet.png), then one body of nearly constant size to t~100 (occupancy ~0.1), then runaway growth to 90% of the domain, substrate depletion and extinction by t~260 (rerun/L040_s8 and L040_s7, T=600, 0 components at the end). So the finding's end states hold, but discrete cells do exist transiently in a narrow window; they are metastable, never divide persistently (0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.8-1.2) and end all-or-nothing.

observations.negative: rerun/p050_s7/sheet.png: default a_th=0.5, cells gone by t=17; rerun/p030_s7/sheet.png: a_th=0.3, one sea with gel foci from t=27; rerun/L040_s8/sheet.png + timeseries.png: a_th=0.4, one cell t=25-106, sea t=131-207, extinct t>=262

seeds_run.result: pass (all-or-nothing end state at every a_th; transient discrete cells at a_th=0.4)

by_construction: phi=0 is absorbing: gel is made only where phi>0, so a dead domain cannot recover
verdicts.limitation: The finding's wording 'never discrete cells' is too strong: at a_th=0.40 a population of 2-4 discrete cells and then a single bounded cell persists for about 100 time units on both fresh seeds before the boom-bust. They do not divide persistently and the end state is still all-or-nothing, so the negative stands. Only a_th was varied; tilt, r, zeta and lt were left at their defaults.
